sourceCopy.examplesHeading: Four useful ways to get started

examples.heading: One ordinary die
examples.text: Draw one integer from 1 through 6. Any of the six faces is a valid result.

examples.heading: Every face without a repeat
examples.text: Draw six unique integers from 1 through 6. Every face appears once, in a random order.

examples.heading: Hundredths from zero to one
examples.text: Draw three values on the 0.01 grid between 0 and 1. Both endpoints are possible.

examples.heading: A range above Number precision
examples.text: Draw two unique integers from 9007199254740993 through 9007199254741993 without rounding the bounds.

steps.heading: Choose the question
steps.text: Select the mode that matches your task. The input labels follow that choice.

steps.heading: Enter the values
steps.text: Both usable endpoints are included. Integer bounds round inward; decimals use the selected grid. Count must be a positive integer.

steps.heading: Check the result
steps.text: Calculate, inspect the working and save the result if needed. Cancel stops a long job.

method.heading: The method behind this result
paragraphs: Random bytes come from the browser’s cryptographic random generator. A rejection step discards values outside the required range. Applying a remainder directly to an arbitrary range can favour some outcomes, so this implementation avoids that modulo bias.

Whole-number mode includes the first and last usable integers. A lower bound of 1.2 becomes 2, while an upper bound of 5.8 becomes 5. If the inward-rounded interval contains no integer, the page explains that the range is empty.

Decimal mode samples a uniform grid, not every possible real number. Two decimal places define steps of 0.01. The bounds are rounded inward to that grid, and both usable endpoints are included. Decimal-grid spacing is an explicit output choice rather than an input-digit ceiling.

Prevent repeats uses a sparse shuffle of the available positions. It keeps only positions needed by the requested draw instead of constructing the entire range. Asking for more unique values than the range contains is impossible and is rejected immediately.

Large bounds remain exact integer or rational values. A range above 4.29 billion is not rejected merely because it exceeds a 32-bit counter. There is no one-hundred-result quota. List storage and output still depend on the device’s real memory.

The generator runs in a worker and can be cancelled. Output appears only after a complete result is ready. A copied share link restores the settings, not a random seed or the same draw. Generate again to obtain a fresh result.

uses.heading: Use the result with the right assumptions
paragraphs: Use a single draw for a die, a sample position or a classroom prompt. Use a no-repeat draw when every selected position should be different. Repeated values are expected when repeats are allowed and the range is small.

For fair decisions involving real participants, agree the range, participant mapping and draw procedure before generating. This page does not provide an independently audited draw record or prove what settings a person used earlier.

Browser cryptography supplies the random bytes, but the page is not a password or cryptographic-key format generator. Use the dedicated password tool when its task is what you need. No paid entropy service or calculation API is contacted.

privacy.heading: Private calculations, clear limits
paragraphs: Your inputs and results stay in this browser. Calculation runs in a local worker, without a calculation API or uploaded data.
The page saves only your theme preference. A copied link contains the selected inputs and options, so share it deliberately.
Large calculations depend on device time and memory. Cancel stops the active job. An error clears old answers and disables their downloads.

faq.question: Are both endpoints included?
faq.answer: Yes, when they lie on the usable integer or decimal grid. Bounds are rounded inward to the selected grid.

faq.question: Can I prevent duplicates?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose Prevent repeats. The requested count must not exceed the number of available grid values.

faq.question: Why is my unique request rejected?
faq.answer: The range contains fewer distinct values than the count requested. Widen the bounds, reduce the count or allow repeats.

faq.question: Is this a continuous decimal distribution?
faq.answer: No. Decimal mode samples a fixed grid, such as hundredths. Each available grid position has the same draw probability.

faq.question: Where does the randomness come from?
faq.answer: The browser’s cryptographic random generator supplies bytes. Rejection sampling maps those bytes to the selected range without modulo bias.

faq.question: Can it generate more than 100 results?
faq.answer: Yes. There is no fixed result-count quota. Large lists consume device memory and can be cancelled before completion.

faq.question: Can the range exceed 32-bit integers?
faq.answer: Yes. Large bounds use exact integers, including values beyond the safe JavaScript Number range.

faq.question: Will a share link reproduce my draw?
faq.answer: No. It restores the settings. A fresh random draw occurs when the page calculates again.

faq.question: Can all values in a unique draw appear?
faq.answer: Yes. Requesting every value gives a random ordering of the finite range, with each value occurring once.

faq.question: Does this prove an official prize draw was fair?
faq.answer: No. It supplies a local random calculation, not an independent audit trail or a verified public draw procedure.
